body.p: Applicant submits this Reply in response to the Office Action mailed November 18, 2024.
I. Status of the Claims
By this Reply, Applicant cancels claim 24 without prejudice or disclaimer, and

amends claims 21-23, 25, 28, 36, and 40. The originally filed specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended claims. Claims 21-23 and 25-40 are pending in this application. Claims 21, 36, and 40 are the sole independent claims.
Applicant thanks the Examiner for the indication of allowable subject matter in claims 24-28, 32, 35, and 37-39.
II. Obiection to the Specification
In the Office Action, the specification was objected to for a minor informality.

(Office Action at p. 2.) In view of the amendment to paragraph [001] of the specification submitted herein to address this informality, withdrawal of the objection is requested. III. Obiection to the Claims
In the Office Action, claim 21 was objected to for a minor informality. (Office
Action at p. 2.) In view of the amendment to claim 21 submitted herein to address this informality, withdrawal of the objection is requested. IV. Section 102 Rejections

In the Office Action, claims 21, 29-31, 33, and 34 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by Diamantopoulos (US 2005/0148903). (Office Action at pp. 3-4.) Claims 21-23, 36, and 40 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as
allegedly being anticipated by Sartor et al. (US 2017/0280970). (Office Action at pp. 4- 6.) Applicant respectfully disagrees and traverses this rejection.

Independent claim 21 as-amended incorporates the subject matter of claim 24 indicated as allowable. Accordingly, Applicant submits that independent claim 21, and any dependent claims thereof, are not anticipated by Diamantopoulos or Sartor, and are allowable.

Independent claim 36 as-amended incorporates subject matter similar to that of allowable claim 32 and intervening claim 31. Accordingly, Applicant submits that independent claim 36, and any dependent claims thereof, are not anticipated by Sartor, and are allowable.

Independent claim 40 as-amended incorporates subject matter similar to that of allowable claim 39. Accordingly, Applicant submits that independent claim 40 is not anticipated by Sartor, and is allowable.
Applicant requests withdrawal of these rejections. V. Conclusion

The Office Action contains characterization of the claims and the related art with which the Applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, Applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be

understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.

In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
If the Examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution,
the Examiner is invited to call Applicant's undersigned representative at (202) 987-7221.

Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5906. In addition, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees due and any other fees due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 during the pendency of this application to Deposit Account No. 50-5906.
Respectfully submitted,
